true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. Because `e.origin` has no trailing slash and `discourseUrl` is expected to end with one, an origin that is a prefix of the configured URL (e.g. `http://discourse.example.co` when `discourseUrl` is `http://discourse.example.com/`, or `http://disc`) passes the check. Any such page that can get itself framed or opened by the blog can then resize the comments iframe arbitrarily. Compare the origin exactly (parse `discourseUrl` and compare `protocol + '//' + host`).

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
X-Frame-Options set to non-standard value "ALLOWALL"

`ALLOWALL` is not a defined `X-Frame-Options` value (only `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, `ALLOW-FROM` exist). Framing only works because browsers ignore an invalid header and fall back to allowing framing; this is undocumented behavior and some user agents/proxies log errors or treat unknown values differently. Since the goal is to permit framing by `embeddable_host`, the header should be removed (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`) or set to `ALLOW-FROM <embeddable_host>` rather than relying on an invalid value being ignored.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Embed URL interpolated unescaped into stored raw HTML (stored XSS) `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the post contents without any HTML/attribute escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `cooked == raw` and Discourse's sanitizer never runs on it. The `url` reaches this code from the `embed_url` request parameter: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any string, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only requires that `URI(url).host` equals `embeddable_host` — the path and query string are unrestricted, and `'`, `=`, `(`, `)` are all valid URI characters. A request such as `/embed/best?embed_url=http:///some-page?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a forged Referer) causes the page to be fetched successfully (query ignored by the origin server) and imported; `absolutize_urls` then re-serializes the broken anchor via Nokogiri into ``, which is persisted and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in both the embed iframe and the normal topic page for every visitor. The URL must be escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`h`) in both the href attribute and the link text.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is a typo that only parses by accident

The closing tag of the header conditional is `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Erubis emits this as `end if` followed by a newline and the next generated `@output_buffer.safe_append='...'` statement, so Ruby parses the whole if/else as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the whitespace-append call. It happens to work today (the append returns a truthy string), but the block body now executes after the following text is appended, and any change to the surrounding template (e.g. removing the blank line or following it with another `<% %>` statement) turns it into a SyntaxError. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs do not render views, so this template is never exercised by tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
poll_feed crashes on RSS 2.0 items because i.content is nil

`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS only populates `item.content` for an actual `<content>` tag (Atom); RSS 2.0 feeds put the body in `description` or `content:encoded` (exposed as `item.content_encoded`), so `i.content` is `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the job has `retry: false` and the exception is unrescued, the first such item aborts the whole poll and no items from the feed are imported, despite the setting being described as an "RSS/ATOM feed". There should be a fallback (`i.content || i.content_encoded || i.description`) and a nil guard. Note also that `String#scrub` only exists on Ruby >= 2.1; if the project still supports Ruby 2.0 this line fails on every item.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Already-shipped migration modified to add force: true

`create_table :top_topics` in an existing, previously-committed migration was changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so anyone who re-runs or rolls back/re-applies this migration (or has a `top_topics` table from a different source) will lose that table's data. Editing migrations that have already been released is also unrelated to this PR's purpose; if the intent is idempotent setup, that should be a new migration or handled in `db:reset`, not a retroactive edit.

Anonymous requests can create unlimited topics and outbound fetches via distinct embed_url values

For any `embed_url` not yet known, `best` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job that fetches the URL over HTTP and creates a new topic (as `embed_by_username`) via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. The only protections are (a) the Referer host check in `ensure_embeddable`, which is trivially forged by any non-browser client, and (b) `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, whose Redis key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` — i.e. per exact URL. Since `TopicEmbed` matches on the exact `embed_url` string, an attacker can request `http://<embeddable_host>/article?1`, `?2`, `?3`, ... and every variant passes the host check, triggers an outbound HTTP fetch (plus, when `feed_polling_enabled`, a synchronous download and processing of the whole RSS feed inside the job via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), and creates a brand new topic. This allows unbounded topic spam and request amplification against the embeddable host with no authentication. At minimum the embed URL should be normalized (strip query/fragment or canonicalize) and there should be a global/host-level rate limit on retrievals and topic creation, not just a per-URL one.

Controller specs assert only `should_not be_success` and never exercise key paths

The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" runs with the default blank `embeddable_host`, so the request is rejected by the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached; the assertion `response.should_not be_success` passes for the wrong reason and does not check the status code. Similarly "raises an error with a missing host" and "raises an error with no referer" don't distinguish which rule fired. Because rspec controller specs do not render views, `best.html.erb` (including the `end if` typo and `@topic_view.topic.url` usage) and `loading.html.erb` are never rendered by any test. Assert specific status codes and add view-rendering (or request) specs for the success paths.

Disqus importer silently drops --category option and original thread dates

The `--category/-c` option was removed and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to pass `category` or `created_at`. Existing users of the thor task passing `-c` will now get an unknown-option error, and all imported topics are created with the current time instead of `Date.parse(t[:created_at])` as before, losing the original thread chronology. Additionally `import_remote` calls `open(url)` before `import` validates the URL scheme, so a thread whose `link` is blank or non-HTTP raises (`Errno::ENOENT`/`OpenURI::HTTPError`) and aborts the whole import run instead of being skipped. These behavior changes are not mentioned in the PR.

Loading page reloads forever when retrieval can never succeed

The loading view reloads itself every 30 seconds unconditionally, and every reload hits `EmbedController#best`, which enqueues another `retrieve_topic` Sidekiq job. If the embed can never be resolved (e.g. `embed_by_username` is blank or points to a missing user, the embed URL host does not match, the remote page 404s, or the import keeps failing), `TopicRetriever` silently returns and the iframe polls indefinitely on every open tab of every blog page, generating a steady stream of requests and queued jobs with no error state ever shown. There should be a cap on retries/time or an error view, and the controller should not enqueue a job on every single poll.

Throttle key SETNX/EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent

`retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or Redis connection drops between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is created with no TTL and never expires, so every subsequent non-staff retrieval for that URL is treated as throttled forever and the embed stays stuck on the loading page. Use a single atomic command (`SET key 1 NX EX 60`, or `setex` guarded by a Lua script) so the TTL is always attached.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (//host/path)

`absolutize_urls` treats every `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `"#{prefix}/#{value.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and blog HTML) also starts with `/`, and the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` — a non-existent URL on the wrong host. All protocol-relative images and links in imported content will therefore be broken. The check should exclude values starting with `//` (or use `URI.join(url, value)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

import checks post.present? instead of post errors/persisted?

`PostCreator#create` returns the `@post` object even when saving failed (e.g. `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` for an untrusted `embed_by_username` user), with errors set and no `id`. `import` only checks `post.present?`, so it proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id, ...)` with `post_id = nil`, which violates the `null: false` constraint and raises a database error out of the job rather than a meaningful failure, and the method may return a post object that was never persisted to its caller (`import_remote`/disqus import then uses `post.topic_id`). Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and return nil (or raise a descriptive error) when creation failed.

poll_feed body (feed parsing and import) has no test coverage

Every example stubs `poll_feed` itself; none exercise the actual parsing in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS item handling, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, calling `TopicEmbed.import`). As a result the `nil.scrub` crash for RSS 2.0 feeds and the entity-unescaping behaviour are untested. A fixture Atom feed and an RSS 2.0 feed (with `description`/`content:encoded`) fed through `poll_feed` with `open` stubbed would catch these.

raw_html cook method bypasses the sanitizer entirely for imported content

With `cook_method == raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, so nothing in Discourse's sanitization pipeline runs. In the RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed`) the feed item HTML is passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with no filtering at all, so `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` links, etc. in the feed go straight into `cooked` and are rendered with `raw post.cooked`. In the HTTP path, `Readability::Document` is given a tag/attribute whitelist, but ruby-readability does not validate attribute values, so `href="javascript:..."` and `src` pointing anywhere survive. This makes every visitor's security depend on the full integrity of the embeddable host's page content and the feed (including any user-generated fragments on those pages). The imported HTML should still be run through the existing sanitizer (or a whitelist that validates URL schemes) before being stored as cooked.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`align-items()` mixin is inconsistent with `flexbox()`: missing `-moz-box-align`, includes a non-existent `-ms-align-items`, and legacy keyword mapping is wrong for flex-start/flex-end

`flexbox()` and `order()` emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, so any Firefox build that only understands `display: -moz-box` gets the flex layout without the vertical alignment (e.g. header contents would not be centered). The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a property in any IE/Edge release (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11+ uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output on every page. Finally, both `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use the keywords `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so a future `@include align-items(flex-start)` would silently produce invalid legacy declarations. The current call sites (`center`, `baseline`) are unaffected, but the mixin as written does not deliver the cross-browser fallback it appears to promise.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`order()` mixin passes the standard `order` value straight through to legacy `box-ordinal-group`, whose scale is different

The new `order($val)` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val` alongside standard `order: $val`. The 2009 box model's `box-ordinal-group` is a positive integer with a default of 1, whereas standard `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negatives. With the current call sites (`order(2)`, `order(3)`) relative ordering still happens to be preserved, but any future use of `order(0)` or a negative value will produce an invalid, ignored legacy declaration, and `order(1)` will be treated as "same as default" in legacy engines while moving the item after default siblings in standard engines. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the legacy value should be `$val + 1`; otherwise the legacy declarations should be dropped rather than emitting misleading output.

false_positives.candidate:
PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make; description is a placeholder

The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and the description is just "Test 5". The change replaces float-based layout in the header, small-action posts and category badges with flexbox and adjusts spacing; nothing in it is a performance optimization (flexbox layout is generally no cheaper than floats, and no measurement is provided). The misleading title and empty description will end up in the commit history and make it hard for anyone bisecting a layout regression (e.g. in `.small-action` or the header `.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` ordering) to understand the intent. The title and description should describe the actual layout change and its visual effects.

`float: right` on `.small-action button` is a no-op now that `.small-action` is a flex container

`.small-action` is converted to `display: flex` (line 264), which makes its direct children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, and the action `button`s) flex items. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the retained `button { float: right; }` (line 309) and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) no longer do anything. Previously the edit/delete buttons on small-action posts were pushed to the right edge by the float; after this change they will sit immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text (which has no `flex: 1` or `margin-left: auto` counterpart) unless some other stylesheet happens to give the description a fixed width. This is a visual regression in the small-action post layout. The fix is to replace the float with `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) and drop the now-dead float declarations.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` overwrites real refresh tokens when spread into stored credentials

When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 264 the data is spread over the existing credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so whenever Microsoft (or the self-hoster's sync endpoint, which per the comments 'should only contain the access token and expiry date') omits a refresh token, the user's real refresh token in the database is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token". Previously, with `refresh_token` optional and absent, the spread left the stored value intact. After this, any later refresh against Microsoft fails permanently and the user must reconnect. true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `z.string().toString()` as keys, which evaluates to "[object Object]" and strips every field except access_token

Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` (ZodType does not override `toString`), so the second overwrites the first and the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. The intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' / 'allow other properties' behaviour does not exist. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, in sharing mode `refreshTokenResponse.data` is `{ access_token }` only: expiry fields are discarded (so Office365's `expires_in` and Zoom's `expires_in` are undefined → `isExpired` stays true and tokens are refreshed on every single API call; Zoom computes `expiry_date = NaN` on line 122 of its adapter and the stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema.parse` on the next load). A permissive schema needs `.passthrough()`/`z.record` or explicit optional fields; this one needs a unit test.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Calendar stores the zod SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Previously this line was `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the token object directly. Now `key` is the wrapper object and it is written to `credential.key` on line 98-101. No tests for the new shared token-parsing/refresh helpers or the webhook endpoint

Trivial tests would have caught that the 'minimum' schema strips every field but `access_token`, that the helper returns the SafeParse wrapper rather than the data (corrupting Google credentials), and that the webhook's `appStoreMetadata[slug]` lookup returns undefined for `google-calendar`. The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` only sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body, with no shared secret, signature or bearer token. The endpoint must therefore hand out live OAuth access tokens for any user id to any caller that can reach it, since the self-hoster has no way to verify the request originated from Cal.com. A `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` pair already exists for the inbound direction; the same header should be sent on this outbound request (and `response.ok` should be checked) so the self-hoster can authenticate it.

Updating an existing credential does not clear the `invalid` flag
